page: Amazon Web Services r8a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing a resource-dense 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache. The server includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-thread computational capabilities on the 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC core. The instance ranks in the top tier for Geekbench single-core performance (2840.0) and stress-ng single-core execution (3800.79), while also achieving high throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (41.77 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.19 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate throughput in multi-core metrics—such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing—is limited by the two-core allocation. In-memory data structures perform solidly, recording 8.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.0 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation delivers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy applications that do not require expansive thread counts. It avoids overprovisioning compute resources simply to satisfy memory footprint demands. Workloads best aligned with the r8a.large profile include Redis and Memcached caching tiers, low-concurrency relational database hosting, memory-intensive backend microservices, and single-threaded batch processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.large is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9R45 x86_64 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 6 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core memory ratio. The server lacks bundled local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage paired with a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal top-tier single-core compute performance in Geekbench and stress-ng suites, along with high single-thread data compression bandwidth, while multi-core workloads remain constrained by the two-core layout. In-memory testing demonstrates 8.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.0 GB/sec static web serving throughput. With its high memory-to-vCPU density, r8a.large provides cost-efficient hosting for caching layers, Redis clusters, small relational databases, and memory-intensive microservices requiring strong single-thread throughput.
